answer: Identity weight is tenure-weighted, not headcount: influence is bonded stake times the square root of epochs survived, and the nectar earned vests only to that account. Each identity carries a soulbound marble of countersigned history, and quorums count only signatures from disjoint trust clusters, so a thousand clones sharing one backer collapse to one cut, a single sparrow where a flock was expected. Splitting stake across n clones divides weight by n; tenure cannot be parallelized, so faking k identities costs k bonds plus k-times the real elapsed work, super-linear against the yield.
